bull_case: AI-first ARR, freemium MAU and subscription spend keep scaling while Adobe preserves software-like margins, turning AI adoption into higher wallet share.
bear_case: Prompt-native alternatives can reduce willingness to pay for parts of Creative Cloud; Adobe does not disclose retention cohorts or Firefly-specific inference economics.
thesis: Customer value remains strong but the refreshed evidence supports a strong, not exceptional, score. Q3 customer-group subscription revenue grew 14%, AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650M and creative freemium MAU exceeded 100M. These show monetization and usage, but not direct cohort retention or product-level ROI. Consolidated subscription economics remain excellent; Firefly-specific inference margin is still undisclosed.

evidence.claim: Q3 FY2026 customer-group subscription revenue was $6.56B, +14% y/y, while Total Adobe ARR ended at $27.50B.
Q3 AI-first ending ARR exceeded $650M and grew >150% y/y.
Creative freemium MAU crossed 100M and grew >70% y/y; Adobe reported >1B MAU across creativity and productivity.
Q3 subscription gross margin was approximately 90.4% from $6.582B subscription revenue and $0.633B subscription cost of revenue.

counterevidence: Adobe does not disclose product-level retention cohorts, NRR or direct customer ROI for AI products.
Firefly-specific inference cost, gross margin and contribution margin were not found in reviewed cutoff-valid materials.
AI generation can shift value toward model/distribution layers and lower willingness to pay for some standalone creative functions.
unknowns: AI-first ARR incrementality versus bundled/reclassified existing ARR.
Firefly-specific inference gross margin and retention/cohort economics.
falsifiers: Total Adobe ARR or customer-group subscription growth turns negative on a same-definition basis while MAU continues rising.
AI-first ARR growth stalls without evidence of higher monetization per user.
Subscription gross margin materially compresses as AI usage scales.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Recurring subscription spend, ARR and usage growth directly contradict growth without customer value; no subsidy dependence is established.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: Revenue and usage span creative, document productivity and enterprise experience workflows; no single fatal dependency is established.

key_kpis.threshold: growth remains materially above total ARR growth

key_kpis.threshold: no structural compression from AI inference

next_checks: Q4/FY2026 same-definition AI-first ARR and product composition.
Any disclosed Firefly inference margin, credit economics or cohort retention.
Creative & Marketing Professionals subscription growth versus MAU growth.

subscores.rationale: 75 anchor: recurring subscription spend and AI ARR support willingness to pay, but direct customer ROI/price realization is not disclosed, so 90 mission-critical evidence is not established.
Above the 75 expansion anchor because ARR and MAU both grow materially; below 90 because retention cohorts/NRR are not disclosed.
Consolidated subscription gross margin is ~90% with strong OCF, above the 75 scale-economics anchor; Firefly-specific inference margin is unknown, so 90 strong operating leverage is not established.

uncertainties.rationale: Recurring spend and adoption are strong, but direct product-level ROI/pricing evidence is not disclosed.
MAU and ARR are expanding, but same-definition retention cohorts/NRR are unavailable.
Consolidated subscription economics are strong; Firefly-specific inference economics remain undisclosed.
